page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 31 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 7.75 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance utilizes an x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The CPU features a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. Storage is bundled via a single local NVMe SSD providing 137 GB of capacity, while no GPUs are present.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average single-core capabilities and weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, alongside a top-tier result in Geekbench text processing. However, multi-core scaling is limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, registering as weak for small block reads and poor for large block uncached reads. For lightweight LLM inference, the server maintains average speeds on a 135M model, but drops to a poor rating for text generation on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4-lssd offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with fast local NVMe storage, making it suitable for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity without massive parallel processing needs. Given its strong single-threaded compression performance and average Redis SET operations, this instance is well-suited for in-memory caching, text processing, lightweight database operations, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks. It is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
